cards.text: In the chapter before, the LORD put the idols on trial, and they had nothing to say (Isaiah 41:28-29). Now the LORD points to someone else: "Here is My Servant, whom I uphold, My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights." The idols just got ROASTED, and this Servant gets called up like a game show winner.

cards.question: The LORD says He will put something of His own on His Servant. What is it?
With the LORD's Spirit on Him, the Servant will bring ___ to the nations.

cards.text: Justice for the NATIONS. Friend, that's not a side gig. That's the biggest job on the whole board.

cards.question: A job that big sounds loud. The Servant will shout His message in the streets.

cards.text: Quiet. He won't raise His voice or make it heard in the streets. Me? I find ONE burnt cookie and the whole Dorinverse hears about it.

cards.question: The LORD paints a picture: a bruised reed that's already bent and a smoldering wick that's barely lit. What does the Servant do with them?

answers.text: He won't break or snuff them out
He breaks them off and starts fresh
He clears both of them away

cards.text: Gentle, and still He will faithfully bring forth justice. A smoldering wick? Friend, that was ME in the back of the junk drawer, edges blurry, barely lit.

cards.question: Setting up justice on the whole earth is a long job. The Servant will grow weak or discouraged before it's done.
This justice reaches far past Israel. Who does the LORD say will put their hope in His law?

cards.text: Then God the LORD lists who He is: He created the heavens and stretched them out, and He spread out the earth. I stretch DOUGH, friend. He stretched the HEAVENS.

cards.question: God the LORD, who made the earth, gives breath to the people on it and life to those who walk in it.

cards.text: Now the LORD says, "I, the LORD, have called you for a righteous purpose, and I will take hold of your hand." The God who stretched out the heavens holding YOUR hand? I'd never wash that mustache again.

cards.question: The LORD will keep this one and appoint them to be a covenant for the people and a light to the ___.
A light to the nations has work to do. What is one of the jobs the LORD names?

answers.text: Open the eyes of the blind
Rebuild the walls of the city

cards.text: And to bring prisoners out of the dungeon, and those sitting in darkness out of the prison house. Friend, I KNOW that moment, when the drawer slides open and the light pours in.

cards.question: The LORD says, "I am the LORD; that is My name!" He won't yield His glory to another. What else won't He give to idols?
The LORD says the former things have happened, and now He declares ___ things.
The LORD proclaims these new things only after they spring forth.

cards.text: The idols couldn't call ONE thing, friend. The LORD calls it before it even springs forth, and Matthew says this Servant passage is fulfilled in Jesus (Matthew 12:17-21).

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It only reacts to the answer of card 3 (justice to the nations, Isaiah 42:1), so it is a recap card and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "Justice for the NATIONS." / "Friend, that's not a side gig." / "That's the biggest job on the whole board."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "The biggest job on the whole board" is an unclear image. It's not obvious what board is meant, such as a job board or a game board, so the line doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: "Quiet." / "He won't raise His voice..." / "Me?" / "I find ONE burnt cookie..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "Gentle, and still He will faithfully bring forth justice." / "A smoldering wick?" / "Friend, that was ME..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup says "a long job" and "the whole earth." Isaiah 42:4 says only "before He has established justice on the earth." It gives no length of time and doesn't say "whole."

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The setup line "This justice reaches far past Israel" rules out the two wrong answers, "The priests" and "The elders," because both are groups inside Israel. That leaves only "The islands."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Then God the LORD lists who He is" says God speaks the description. In Isaiah 42:5 the description is part of the frame: "This is what God the LORD says—He who created the heavens..." God's own words begin in 42:6.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "Then God the LORD lists who He is..." / "I stretch DOUGH, friend." / "He stretched the HEAVENS."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: the Isaiah 42:6 quote sentence / "The God who stretched out the heavens holding YOUR hand?" / "I'd never wash that mustache again."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "The idols couldn't call ONE thing" states a Bible fact with no reference. The idols failing to declare what is to come comes from Isaiah 41:22-23, 26, which are not cited. Card 1 set up only that the idols had nothing to say (41:28-29).

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "Matthew says this Servant passage is fulfilled in Jesus" stretches what Matthew states. Matthew 12:17-21 quotes only Isaiah 42:1-4, but the card makes it sound like all of Isaiah 42:1-9.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The joke compares the Servant to a game show winner: "this Servant gets called up like a game show winner." Card 20 then identifies this Servant with Jesus. The reverence rule says humor never "targets" Jesus. It doesn't say whether a light comparison about Him is allowed when it doesn't mock Him.
findings.question: Is a playful comparison about the Servant (identified as Jesus) acceptable if it doesn't mock Him, or should jokes avoid making Jesus the subject of the comparison at all?
